challenges.name: menu-refresh-bounded-fanout
challenges.title: Refresh 300 partner menus with bounded fan-out
challenges.description: Every morning Rice Rocket refreshes the menus of its partner restaurants. The first version awaited them one by one (two minutes); the second started all 300 with `asyncio.gather`, the partner gateway answered 429 to everything over 20 open calls, and one broken restaurant failed the whole batch. The editor holds `refresh_menus` with its key lines missing, each marked by a `# [ ]` line; some pieces are wrong on purpose. Fill every line so that at most `limit` calls are open at once, all restaurants run concurrently up to that limit, a failing restaurant becomes `{"error": ...}` without stopping the others, and the result keeps the input order. Run refreshes the test's restaurants on a simulated clock and reports the most calls open at once, the time it took and the failures.
hints: Count open calls at the busiest moment: which object is shared by all the calls, and where is it created? A limit that every call creates for itself limits nothing.
Look at `asyncio.Semaphore(limit)` created once, `async with slots:` around exactly the partner call, a `try/except PartnerError` per restaurant, and `asyncio.gather` (results in argument order).

Thumbnails for 1,000 photos with at most 8 uploads at a time: `slots = asyncio.Semaphore(8)` once; `async def upload(p): async with slots: return await cdn.put(p)`; `async def safe(p): try: return {"ok": await upload(p)} except CdnError as e: return {"error": str(e)}`; `await asyncio.gather(*(safe(p) for p in photos))`.

tests.name: 25 restaurants, limit 10: never more than 10 open calls, done in 3 rounds
All 300 partners: no 429 from the gateway, 30 rounds of 10
Two restaurants are down: their errors are listed, the other menus arrive
Limit 1 for a fragile partner: one call at a time
